# Half Hourly Insights

> A free tool for analysing UK half-hourly (HH) electricity meter data. Load one Excel or CSV file per meter and see out-of-hours use priced at your rates, base load, peaks against agreed supply capacity, unusual days and lasting changes, with savings scenarios, PDF and Excel reports and password-protected customer dashboards.

Operated by Kinetic Energy Consulting. Free to use, no sign-up. The analyser runs entirely in the browser: meter data is never uploaded.

Scope: UK businesses and public sector organisations. Results are indicative estimates from the data loaded: costs are energy cost at the rates entered, not guaranteed savings, and whole-site data shows when energy is used, not which equipment uses it. The method is set out on the How it works page.

Method in brief: base load is the 5th percentile of valid half-hourly demand; out-of-hours (closed-hours) excess is energy used outside the opening hours above that base load; missing readings are left out, never counted as zero; annual figures are scaled from valid hours and withheld under 180 days of data; kVA is kW divided by an assumed power factor.

## Tool

- [Analyser](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/analyser/): the tool itself, in the browser.

## Core pages

- [Free business electricity analysis](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/): What the analyser shows, the three steps, and the privacy model (analysis runs in the browser).
- [How it works](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/how-it-works): The method in full: reading files, data checks, opening hours, base load (5th percentile), closed-hours excess, costs, annualisation, findings, capacity, and limits.
- [Questions and answers](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/faq): Cost, privacy, the data needed and what the results mean.
- [Contact](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/contact): Enquiries to Kinetic Energy Consulting, which runs the site.
- [Sample half-hourly electricity report for an office](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/sample-report): A sample report for a made-up office: 33% of use while closed, £2,776 a year above base load, base load 2.6 kW, findings and what could be saved.
- [About Half Hourly Insights and Paul Johnston](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/about): Who runs the site (Kinetic Energy Consulting, Managing Director Paul Johnston), why the analyser is free, and how the guides are sourced and checked.

## Guides

- [How to get your half-hourly electricity data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/get-your-data): Who holds half-hourly data, what to ask your supplier for, the file layouts the analyser reads, and what to do if your supplier cannot provide it.
- [Worked example: a year of half-hourly data for one office](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/example-office-analysis): A small office run through the analyser: 33% of use while closed, £2,776 a year above base load, almost half on Saturdays; base load 2.6 kW; 67% of a 40 kVA supply.
- [Out-of-hours electricity use: how to find and cut it](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/out-of-hours-electricity): What out-of-hours electricity use is, how to find it in half-hourly data (opening hours, heatmap, day types, start and end of the day), common causes, fixes and who to involve.
- [Base load electricity: what it is and how to cut it](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/base-load): What base load is, how to measure it from half-hourly data (5th percentile, not the minimum), what makes it up, how to reduce it; 1 kW all year is 8,760 kWh.
- [Supply capacity and kVA: room for heat pumps and EVs](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/supply-capacity): Agreed supply capacity in kVA, kW to kVA via power factor, headroom from half-hourly peaks with a safety margin, and checking heat pumps and EV charging.
- [Worked example: a primary school's half-hourly data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/example-school-analysis): A primary school with term dates entered: 31% of use while closed, £1,261 a year above base load; heating left on through October half term (demand more than double); evening lettings.
- [How to read a half-hourly electricity heatmap](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/reading-a-heatmap): How to read a half-hourly heatmap (days across, time of day down, colour for demand) and the patterns that point to waste.
- [How to prove an energy saving worked, with half-hourly data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/proving-savings): Proving a saving with half-hourly data: matched before-and-after periods, the right measure for the change, weather effects, and the analyser tools.
- [Market-wide half-hourly settlement (MHHS) explained](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-settlement): Market-wide half-hourly settlement: Ofgem decision 20 April 2021; migration began 21 October 2025, due complete 7 May 2027; four-month settlement timetable from 2 July 2027; microbusinesses cannot opt out.
- [Glossary of half-hourly electricity terms](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/glossary): Definitions: base load, closed-hours excess, kW, kWh, kVA, power factor, MPAN, agreed supply capacity, settlement, MHHS, heatmap, load factor and more.
- [Guides to half-hourly electricity data](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/guides): Index of guides.
- [Half-hourly electricity data from British Gas Business](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-data-british-gas): British Gas Business half-hourly data: Energy360 DataView (free, smart meter customers, request via chat, login within 10 working days); brokers need authorisation; up to 12 months free on request under government rules.
- [Half-hourly electricity data from EDF (business)](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-data-edf): EDF business half-hourly data: MyBusiness Data Analysis (4 MPANs) and Data Export (up to 350,000 records, about 20 MPANs for a year, CSV or Excel); small business Energy Hub with smart meter data preference set to half-hourly.
- [Half-hourly electricity data from E.ON Next](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-data-eon-next): E.ON Next business half-hourly data: no self-service download described publicly; profile class 00 check; data collector holds readings; Optimum included with E.ON data collection; up to 12 months free on request.
- [Half-hourly data from npower Business Solutions](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-data-npower-business-solutions): npower Business Solutions half-hourly data: Dashboard Meters section, "Download Half-Hourly (HH) data consumption", last 12 months; or email the Metering Team at nbssmart@npower.com.
- [Half-hourly electricity data from TotalEnergies](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/half-hourly-data-totalenergies): TotalEnergies Gas & Power half-hourly data: TotalEnergies Insights portal (from 1 October 2024, up to 12 months, smart and AMR meters not half-hourly settled, profile classes 1-8); access via the Half-Hourly Data Request Form.
- [Reading your MPAN: profile class and network region](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/mpan-profile-class): The MPAN supply number: bottom line is the 13-digit MPAN (distributor ID 10-23 identifies the network region, unique reference, check digit); top line profile class 00-08, MTC, LLFC; under MHHS profile classes are removed and migrated meters show 00.
- [Electricity benchmarks by sector: kWh per m² a year](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/electricity-benchmarks): Electricity benchmarks per m² (gross internal area) by sector from BEES 2014-15: offices median 88 kWh/m² (with other fuels) or 124 (all-electric); full quartile ranges for nine sectors; DEC operational rating 100 is typical, based on CIBSE TM46 benchmarks.
- [What's in a business electricity price?](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/business-electricity-price): Components of a UK business electricity price; worked 2026/27 example for a 500 MWh site: published network and policy charges about 9.3p/kWh, about a third of the 27.67p/kWh average delivered price (DESNZ, Q2 2026).
- [Non-energy charges on business electricity bills, explained](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/non-energy-charges): Non-energy charges explained with 2026/27 rates: TNUoS bands (LV1-LV4 £5.80-£38.18/site/day), DUoS time bands, BSUoS £13.74/£12.49/MWh, RO £32.73/MWh, CfD £0-£10.56/MWh, Capacity Market (4-7pm winter working days), nuclear RAB, FiT, CCL 0.801p/kWh, VAT.
- [UK business electricity prices, 2015 to 2026](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/electricity-prices-ten-years): UK business electricity prices 2015-2025 by size band (DESNZ QEP 3.4.2): 500-1,999 MWh band 10.9p (2015), 15.8p (2021), 32.2p (2023), 28.3p/kWh (2025); wholesale history from Ofgem; drivers: wind, gas and carbon, European prices.
- [Where non-energy electricity costs are heading from 2027](https://halfhourlyinsights.netlify.app/non-energy-costs-outlook): Outlook for UK non-energy electricity costs: BSUoS draft £21.67/MWh (Apr-Sep 2027) and £18.42/MWh (Oct 2027-Mar 2028); RO 0.369 ROC/MWh 2027/28 (0.394 with BICS); CCL 0.827p/kWh from April 2027 then frozen; CfD £2.98/MWh Q1 2027; ED3 network price control from 2028.
